title: GB News is allowed to promote Reform, so I’m setting up Woke TV
gist: Alan Rusbridger satirically responds to new Ofcom chair Sir Ian Cheshire's suggestion that he and Stewart Purvis start a left-wing GB News, using it to attack Ofcom's weak impartiality enforcement against GB News and its promotion of Reform.

insights.claim: New Ofcom chair Sir Ian Cheshire told MPs he would encourage Stewart Purvis and Alan Rusbridger to set up a left-wing version of GB News, which Rusbridger reads as tacit concession that GB News is a right-wing channel.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Signals a light-touch regulatory stance on broadcaster impartiality under the new chair.
insights.quote: set up the left-wing version of GB News
insights.locator: And after Michael Grade there arose

insights.claim: Rusbridger argues Ofcom's duty is to enforce due impartiality under the law, and that proposing a balancing partisan channel abandons that duty.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Regulatory approach to partisan broadcasting affects the UK media and political landscape for Reform.
insights.locator: You may have thought that Ofcom’s job

insights.claim: The author describes GB News as the dominant Reform TV operation pumping out nightly right-wing propaganda.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Frames GB News as a political vehicle for Reform, relevant to UK political media risk.

insights.claim: The Woke TV proposal is a satirical lineup of left-wing figures mirroring GB News presenters, meant to show the absurdity of balancing partisan channels with opposing partisan channels.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Satire; no operating plan for a real channel is described.
insights.locator: I think we will call it GB Woke
